verdict_reason: The class does its narrow job correctly but its Javadoc asserts a contract-divergence guarantee OperatorComplianceIT does not provide, and it omits the global info/servers/securityScheme declaration that would give the committed spec an identity and reconcile it with the locked contract.

todos.issue: Javadoc claims the ModelResolver stops /v3/api-docs diverging from 'the locked contract - the exact divergence OperatorComplianceIT fails the build on', but that gate (OperatorComplianceIT lines 231-251) compares only path keys, HTTP-method keys and operationIds against docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml; components.schemas, parameters, securitySchemes and info are never compared, so the locked contract's snake_case operator_type/crn/approval_number/transporter_category fields and its Trade-Imports-Crn header pass green despite existing nowhere in the code
todos.fix: Withdraw the overclaim (the resolver only binds swagger-core to the app ObjectMapper) and extend OperatorComplianceIT's divergence gate to also compare components.schemas property-name sets and operation parameter names, so a locked contract documenting fields the service does not implement fails the build

todos.issue: OpenApiConfig declares no @OpenAPIDefinition and no OpenAPI bean, so the spec published at /v3/api-docs and committed as docs/openapi/operators.yml carries springdoc placeholders 'title: OpenAPI definition' and 'version: v0' (operators.yml lines 3-4) with no servers block (OperatorComplianceIT line 210 strips servers before writing) - an untitled, unversioned, base-URL-less artifact that README line 185 advertises as committed 'for downstream consumers', and that contradicts the locked contract's title trade-imports-address-book / version 1.0.0 / servers block
todos.fix: Add @OpenAPIDefinition(info = @Info(title = "trade-imports-address-book", version = "1.0.0", description = ...)) to this class and an @Bean OpenAPI declaring the deployed servers, so the generated document carries real identity and matches api-contract.locked.yaml lines 2-4 and 76

todos.issue: No SecurityScheme is declared here, so the identity contract is documented two incompatible ways and nothing reconciles them: the generated spec models Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id as a per-operation @RequestHeader parameter (operators.yml lines 21/55/104/141/187) while api-contract.locked.yaml lines 376-396 declares securitySchemes Trade-Imports-Crn AND Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id, with Trade-Imports-Crn described as the primary identity header - IdentityHeaderFilter lines 46/73 reads only Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id and 400s otherwise, so a consumer coding to the locked contract sends Trade-Imports-Crn and is rejected
todos.fix: Declare a single apiKey-in-header SecurityScheme for Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id in an @Bean OpenAPI here plus a matching @SecurityRequirement, and delete the Trade-Imports-Crn scheme and its narrative from api-contract.locked.yaml since no code enforces it

todos.issue: new ModelResolver(objectMapper) hands swagger-core the application's singleton ObjectMapper; swagger-core's AbstractModelConverter constructor calls mapper.registerModule(...) which inserts SwaggerAnnotationIntrospector into that mapper, so swagger annotations begin influencing real HTTP serialisation (hasRequiredMarker, findSubtypes, findTypeName) and not just the generated document
todos.fix: Pass a copy - new ModelResolver(objectMapper.copy()) - which keeps the JacksonConfig LOWER_CAMEL_CASE strategy the Javadoc relies on while leaving the runtime mapper unmutated
